packet.headline_seed: Afghan Taliban launch strikes on border with Pakistan as tensions escalate
packet.description_seed: Pakistan's military says it shot down four rudimentary drones and will respond to any further provocation.

what: Afghan Taliban launch strikes on border with Pakistan as tensions escalate

clean_source_blocks.text: Several people were reportedly injured in Pakistan's southwestern Balochistan province. Afghanistan's Taliban regime said they have carried out strikes on targets along the border with Pakistan, injuring several people in Pakistan's southwestern Balochistan province. Pakistan's military said it had shot down four rudimentary drones and warned any further provocation "would receive a befitting response". The BBC has been unable to independently confirm the attack. The strikes come after Pakistan launched its own airstrikes on Afghanistan on Sunday, killing 28 civilians, according to the UN. Tensions have reignited in the region after months of relative calm. The two countries had agreed to a ceasefire in October following weeks of deadly clashes. Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan of harbouring terrorists who carry out attacks on its soil, a claim the Taliban government rejects.

The two countries had agreed to a ceasefire in October following weeks of deadly clashes. Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan of harbouring terrorists who carry out attacks on its soil, a claim the Taliban government rejects.
Pakistan's military says it shot down four rudimentary drones and will respond to any further provocation.

Overnight airstrikes by Pakistani forces have killed at least 36 civilians and injured more than 160 others, Afghan officials said Monday, as tensions between the neighbors further escalated. Pakistani security forces carried out a ground operation along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border late Sunday, followed by strikes against militant hideouts and safe havens, killing 29 fighters, Pakistan’s Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said. They said the operations were launched in response to multiple militant attacks across Pakistan. Afghanistan condemned the strikes as a “cowardly act of aggression” and an “act of brutality.”

Several people were reportedly injured in Pakistan's southwestern Balochistan province.

Afghanistan's Taliban regime said they have carried out strikes on targets along the border with Pakistan, injuring several people in Pakistan's southwestern Balochistan province.

Pakistan's military said it had shot down four rudimentary drones and warned any further provocation "would receive a befitting response". The BBC has been unable to independently confirm the attack.

The strikes come after Pakistan launched its own airstrikes on Afghanistan on Sunday, killing 28 civilians, according to the UN.

Tensions have reignited in the region after months of relative calm. The two countries had agreed to a ceasefire in October following weeks of deadly clashes.

Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan of harbouring terrorists who carry out attacks on its soil, a claim the Taliban government rejects.

Kabul in turn has accused Islamabad of carrying out unprovoked attacks which kill civilians. Pakistan says it only targets militants.

Afghanistan said Pakistan's attack on Sunday hit civilian homes and put the civilian death toll at 36, with more than 160 injured.

It described the attack as a "cowardly act" and an "atrocity".

Pakistan said it had carried out a ground operation along the border and air strikes targeting militant hideouts in Afghanistan's Paktia, Paktika and Kunar provinces.

The country's information minister, Attaullah Tarar, said 29 militants had been killed in an operation responding to "recent terrorist attacks against innocent people".

The BBC has not independently confirmed figures from either side.

Intermittent border clashes and air strikes in the area have killed dozens of people in recent months, according to officials in both countries.

In February, clashes between the two countries left dozens of people dead. In March, a Pakistani strike on a drug rehabilitation centre in Kabul killed hundreds.

Earlier in June, Pakistan launched deadly air strikes that killed 26 militants. Afghanistan's Taliban government said 13 people, mostly children, were also killed in the strikes.

Afghanistan condemned the strikes as a “cowardly act of aggression” and an “act of brutality.”

Hamdullah Fitrat, the deputy spokesman for Afghanistan’s Taliban government, said the Pakistani forces targeted a home in Chamkani district, in Paktia province, killing an elderly man and a child, while other family members were injured. When residents gathered to rescue people, the area was struck again, killing 28 villagers and wounding 158, he said.

Six people, mostly women and children, were killed in a village in Giyan district, Paktika province, when another home was struck, he said. A civilian home in Kunar province was also hit, causing no casualties but killing some 30 livestock.

Militant attacks targeting Pakistan’s police and security forces have surged in recent years. Authorities have blamed the Pakistani Taliban — known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP — and allied militant groups for most of the violence. The Pakistani Taliban are separate from but allied with the Afghan Taliban that returned to power in 2021.

payload.title: Taliban kertoo iskeneensä Pakistanin rajalla jännitteiden kiristyessä
payload.summary: Afganistanin Taliban-hallinto sanoo tehneensä iskuja Pakistanin vastaisella rajalla. Pakistanin armeijan mukaan se pudotti neljä alkeellista droonia ja vastaa uusiin provokaatioihin.
payload.content:
Afganistanin Taliban-hallinto kertoo tehneensä iskuja kohteisiin Pakistanin vastaisella rajalla, ja useiden ihmisten kerrotaan haavoittuneen Pakistanin lounaisessa Balochistanin maakunnassa. Pakistanin armeija sanoo pudottaneensa neljä alkeellista droonia ja varoittaa, että mahdolliset uudet provokaatiot saisivat sen mukaan asianmukaisen vastauksen.

## Iskut seuraavat Pakistanin toimia Afganistanissa

Tilanne rajaseudulla on kiristynyt uudelleen kuukausien suhteellisen rauhallisen jakson jälkeen. Maiden välille sovittiin lokakuussa tulitauko viikkoja kestäneiden, kuolonuhreja vaatineiden yhteenottojen jälkeen.

Talibanin ilmoittamien iskujen taustalla ovat Pakistanin sunnuntaina Afganistaniin tekemät ilmaiskut. YK:n mukaan niissä kuoli 28 siviiliä. Afganistanilaisviranomaisten mukaan Pakistanin joukkojen yön yli jatkuneissa iskuissa kuoli ainakin 36 siviiliä ja yli 160 ihmistä haavoittui. BBC ei ole pystynyt riippumattomasti vahvistamaan Talibanin ilmoittamaa rajaiskua.

## Pakistan perustelee operaatioita militantti-iskuilla

Pakistanin tiedotusministeri Attaullah Tararin mukaan Pakistanin turvallisuusjoukot tekivät myöhään sunnuntaina maaoperaation Pakistanin ja Afganistanin rajalla. Sen jälkeen joukot iskivät militanttien piilopaikkoihin ja tukialueisiin. Tararin mukaan operaatioissa kuoli 29 taistelijaa, ja Pakistanin mukaan toimet käynnistettiin vastauksena useisiin militantti-iskuihin eri puolilla maata.

## Pitkä kiista militanttien suojelusta

Pakistan on pitkään syyttänyt Afganistania siitä, että se sallii Pakistanissa iskuja tekevien terroristien toimia alueellaan. Taliban-hallinto kiistää syytökset ja on tuominnut Pakistanin viimeisimmät iskut jyrkästi. Afganistan kuvasi iskuja pelkurimaiseksi hyökkäykseksi ja raakuudeksi.

Pakistanin armeijan drooniväite ja Talibanin ilmoitus rajaiskuista lisäävät painetta kahden naapurin suhteissa tilanteessa, jossa lokakuun tulitauko on jo ennestään hauras. Vahvistamattomat tiedot iskuista, uhrilukujen erot ja osapuolten vastakkaiset väitteet tekevät kokonaiskuvasta edelleen epäselvän.
summary_bullets: Taliban-hallinto kertoo tehneensä iskuja Pakistanin vastaisella rajalla.
Pakistanin armeijan mukaan se pudotti neljä alkeellista droonia.
Taustalla ovat Pakistanin Afganistaniin tekemät iskut ja pitkä kiista militanttien toiminnasta.
payload.journalist_note: Uhriluvuissa on lähteiden välillä eroja: YK:n mukaan Pakistanin aiemmissa iskuissa kuoli 28 siviiliä, kun taas afganistanilaisviranomaiset ovat ilmoittaneet vähintään 36 siviiliuhrista. Talibanin rajaiskuja ei ole riippumattomasti vahvistettu.
